label: input i late in a y-initial sequence after p/3/o/c/x/t context
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.006% of steps). Fires almost only in the original phase at positions 4-8 (peak at 5-6), with a small tail on the <DEL> step; it never fires in the copy phase. 86% of activation mass is in sequences whose first token is y, and 74% is on steps where the input is i (21x lift). Magnitude is highest when i follows earlier tokens like x, c, p, 3, o, t (the top example is y x 3 c p [i]); prev_tok p (11x) and 3 (5x) carry the strongest lift. The plain rule y-first, input i, position >= 4 has precision of only about 0.12, because most such steps do not fire; adding a requirement of at least 2 earlier tokens from {p,3,o,c,x,t,2,1} raises precision to about 0.3 (dev F1 0.33, mass recall 0.52). Misses: other tokens at the same positions in similar contexts (z, 3, 1, <DEL>) and a few sequences that do not start with y. The exact context dependence looks like a fuzzy conjunction of several prefix tokens that a simple predicate does not capture.
